description: I'm a Grade 10 student and solo developer who built ClimaLens UAE to make NASA climate data easier to explore and understand across the UAE. The platform uses over four decades of NASA POWER data based on the MERRA-2 reanalysis, allowing users to compare selected locations across the country, explore environmental trends and examine statistical evidence using two complementary methods.
summary:
ClimaLens UAE is an interactive web platform built with Python, Flask and NASA POWER meteorological data derived from the MERRA-2 reanalysis. It helps users investigate long-term environmental trends across selected locations in the United Arab Emirates, including Al Ruwais, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Al Ain and Liwa Oasis. The displayed analysis covers 1984–2025.

Climate records contain seasonal cycles, year-to-year fluctuations and extreme observations that can make long-term changes difficult to identify. ClimaLens addresses this by grouping monthly observations into All-Year, Summer and Winter (DJF) baselines and analysing trends using two complementary statistical methods: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression and the non-parametric Mann–Kendall test.

The platform presents trend direction, estimated change per decade, confidence intervals and statistical evidence through interactive visualisations. Its Plain Language / Detailed views make findings accessible to general users while retaining statistical information for deeper investigation.

By combining regional comparisons, statistical analysis and transparent data limitations, ClimaLens UAE connects NASA Earth science data with potential applications in cooling demand, heat exposure, energy planning and environmental resilience.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

ClimaLens UAE is an interactive climate investigation platform developed to help users explore long-term environmental trends across the United Arab Emirates using NASA POWER climate data.

Climate datasets contain seasonal cycles, year-to-year fluctuations and occasional extreme observations. These variations can make it difficult to distinguish long-term changes from short-term variability. ClimaLens addresses this challenge by allowing users to investigate different locations, environmental variables and seasonal periods through interactive visualisations and statistical analysis.

The platform follows three main stages:

1. Seasonal Aggregation

Users can investigate All-Year, Summer and Winter (DJF) conditions. Monthly observations are grouped into the selected seasonal baseline, allowing trends to be examined across different parts of the year rather than relying on a single annual average.

2. Statistical Trend Analysis

Each selected dataset is analysed using two complementary methods:

  • Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression estimates the direction and magnitude of the trend, including its rate of change per decade, 95% confidence interval and associated p-value.
  • The non-parametric Mann–Kendall test evaluates whether the observations show a consistent increasing or decreasing trend over time.

ClimaLens identifies trends supported by both tests at the 0.05 significance level. These results indicate statistical evidence of a trend, not proof of its cause. The analysis also communicates limitations such as potential year-to-year autocorrelation.

3. Regional Comparison and Interpretation

Users can compare locations, examine different climate variables and explore a regional ranking of estimated trend rates. A Plain Language / Detailed interface presents findings at two levels: accessible explanations for general users and statistical information for users interested in the underlying evidence.

2. Key Discoveries & Intended Impact

ClimaLens uses regional analysis to explore how different environmental variables behave across the UAE.

Widespread Temperature Increases

The analysed locations show statistically significant upward trends in mean air temperature under the platform's dual-test criterion. In the displayed analysis, Al Ruwais has an estimated increase of approximately +0.389 °C per decade, while Dubai shows approximately +0.369 °C per decade.

These findings highlight the importance of examining regional temperature trends when discussing long-term cooling demand, heat exposure and infrastructure resilience.

Seasonal Humidity Patterns

The platform allows users to investigate relative humidity across different seasons, including winter conditions along the UAE coast. This provides a basis for exploring environmental patterns relevant to coastal infrastructure and atmospheric conditions.

Rainfall Variability

Precipitation analysis demonstrates the importance of distinguishing individual rainfall fluctuations from sustained long-term trends. Where statistical evidence is insufficient, ClimaLens communicates that a significant trend has not been established rather than presenting fluctuations as a confirmed climate signal.

From Data to Decisions

Beyond presenting statistical results, ClimaLens provides operational interpretations that connect environmental findings to potential planning considerations, including cooling infrastructure, heat exposure and water-resource management.

These interpretations are intended to support further investigation and informed discussion, not replace detailed engineering assessments or local measurements.

3. Tools, Data & Technologies Used

NASA Earth Science Data

ClimaLens uses NASA POWER climate data derived from the MERRA-2 meteorological reanalysis. The analysed variables include:

  • Mean Air Temperature (T2M)
  • Maximum Air Temperature (T2M_MAX)
  • Relative Humidity (RH2M)
  • Corrected Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR)
  • All-Sky Surface Shortwave Downward Irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN)

Backend and Statistical Analysis

  • Python — application logic and data processing.
  • Flask — web application backend.
  • Pandas and NumPy — data processing and numerical calculations.
  • SciPy — linear regression and statistical calculations.
  • pymannkendall — Mann–Kendall trend analysis.

Frontend and Visualisation

  • HTML5 and Tailwind CSS — interface and styling.
  • JavaScript — interactive controls.
  • Plotly.js — interactive charts, trend lines and confidence intervals.
  • Geographic visualisation — regional exploration of UAE locations.

4. Creativity & Scientific Integrity

ClimaLens UAE combines regional climate investigation, statistical analysis and accessible communication in one interactive platform.

Its main distinction is the connection between scientific evidence and practical interpretation. Rather than simply displaying environmental charts, the application helps users investigate the direction and magnitude of trends, examine statistical evidence and understand the limitations behind the results.

The Plain Language / Detailed interface makes the platform accessible to users with different levels of scientific knowledge, while its regional comparison tools encourage exploration beyond a single location.

Scientific transparency is central to the project. NASA POWER provides gridded environmental estimates rather than direct measurements from individual ground stations. Nearby locations may therefore share underlying grid cells, and the results should not be interpreted as precise site-level measurements.

ClimaLens is designed as an exploratory tool for understanding regional environmental patterns and communicating scientific evidence responsibly.
